audit_items.proof_trace: The middleware checks only that `oauth_user_id` and `oauth_access_token` cookies are non-empty strings (`if (oauthUserId && oauthToken) return NextResponse.next()`), never calling the STEM OAuth `/userinfo` endpoint or verifying a JWT signature. Any request with arbitrary non-empty cookie values passes. The `updateSession()` call that does perform server-side validation via `supabase.auth.getUser()` is only reached for public paths (`/login`, `/auth/*`), the exact inverse of what the property requires.
audit_items.attack_scenario: An attacker sends a raw HTTP request to `/api/admin/force-logout-all` with forged headers `Cookie: oauth_user_id=x; oauth_access_token=x`; middleware passes (line 38), the route handler performs no auth check, and `forceLogoutAll()` is executed during the 22:50–23:50 JST window. Separately, a user whose STEM OAuth token has been server-side revoked retains full application access for up to 1 hour (cookie maxAge) because revocation is never checked.
